theme: When the network fails: timeouts, retries and URLError

terms.definition: The longest time a request may wait before the app gives up.
terms.example: Set a timeout of ten seconds for this request.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let u = URL(string: "https://x.com")!
var r = URLRequest(url: u)
r.timeoutInterval = 5
print(r.timeoutInterval)

terms.definition: The step of sending a failed request again, often after a short wait.
terms.example: Add a retry for the weak Wi-Fi case.
terms.code:
var n = 0
func ok() -> Bool { n += 1; return n > 2 }
while !ok() {}   // retry until it works
print("ok after", n)

terms.definition: The error type for network problems, like no internet or a lost connection.
terms.example: Catch the URLError and show a friendly message.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let e = URLError(.notConnectedToInternet)
print(e.code == .notConnectedToInternet)
print(e.errorCode)

Learn to explain handling slow and failed requests: Timeout, Retry & URLError, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Timeout - The longest time a request may wait before the app gives up.
Retry - The step of sending a failed request again, often after a short wait.
URLError - The error type for network problems, like no internet or a lost connection.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Timeout, Retry & URLError in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Timeout, Retry, URLError 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Timeout - The longest time a request may wait before the app gives up.
한국어: Timeout: 앱이 포기하기 전에 요청이 기다릴 수 있는 가장 긴 시간

Retry - The step of sending a failed request again, often after a short wait.
한국어: Retry: 실패한 요청을 보통 잠깐 기다린 뒤 다시 보내는 단계

URLError - The error type for network problems, like no internet or a lost connection.
한국어: URLError: 인터넷이 없거나 연결이 끊긴 것 같은 네트워크 문제의 에러 타입

landscape.hook: Can you explain Timeout, Retry and URLError in English?

dialogue.title: The endless spinner

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, users in the subway see an endless spinner.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Set a timeout. It is the longest time a request may wait before the app gives up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What happens when the timeout ends?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The session throws a URLError with the code `timedOut`, like in our code.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So URLError is the error type for network problems?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes: no internet, a lost connection or a slow request.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Should I show an alert straight away?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: First retry. A retry sends the failed request again, often after a short wait.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How many times should I retry?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Two or three. Then show the error and let the user press a button.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And a retry is only safe for some requests, right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good memory! Retry a GET request, and check the URLError code first.
Set a timeout of ten seconds for this request.
